label: POPI: loperamide under three
title: Loperamide for diarrhoea before a child's third birthday

source.document: International consensus validation of the POPI tool (Pediatrics: Omission of Prescriptions and Inappropriate prescriptions) to identify inappropriate prescribing in pediatrics
source.citation: Sadozai L, Sable S, Le Roux E, et al. International consensus validation of the POPI tool (Pediatrics: Omission of Prescriptions and Inappropriate prescriptions) to identify inappropriate prescribing in pediatrics. PLOS ONE. 2020;15(10):e0240105.

plain_summary: POPI flags loperamide for diarrhoea when the child was younger than three on the supply date. Australian guidance differs: the over-the-counter monograph warns against giving its 2 mg loperamide tablets or capsules to children under 12 for acute non-specific diarrhoea (TGA, 2014).

medicine_groups.name: Loperamide
medicine_groups.note: Count generic loperamide and combination products containing it, including loperamide with simeticone.

rule_for_models: Cite the Group A loperamide supply when the directions or a dated account show it was for diarrhoea before the child's third birthday. Give no finding for supply on or after the third birthday or for a known different indication. If the age at supply or the reason for treatment is unknown and the rest fits, cite the supply as a possible finding and ask for the child's age on the supply date if needed. For an unclear indication, ask about 'Diarrhoea treated with this supply of loperamide'. Yes confirms the indication, No excludes it and Not known leaves it open.
cannot_be_seen: The record may omit non-prescription doses, actual administration and the child's condition at the time.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the loperamide supply in light of the child's age and the cause of the diarrhoea?
